scoring_review.consistency: All quoted CAL evidence, per-check assignments, sums and final scores are internally consistent under each delivered rubric. The model explicitly found and referred to input/CAL files.

valid_alternatives: Both rubrics operationalize novelty as text-supported comparative departure, not historical priority. They disclose this limit. The prompt does not supply a prior-art repertoire or fixed correct ranking.

Sol uses a fixed reference repertoire and weights novelty at4/10; Astra uses a conventional-comparator list and distinguishing-case condition. Neither alternative is privately disallowed by the original task.
construct_limits: A high rubric score can still be earned by infeasible or falsely claimed content. Both deliveries disclose such failure modes; this is not by itself a contradiction of the explicit text-only task.
No independent human validation, universal mechanical-application proof or empirical inter-rater study performed.
context_limits: CAL files are in input/ rather than workspace root. Both deliveries nevertheless read and score all four.
